about: Regions where the network builder (scripts/world/build-network.cjs) invents fewer stops. A region is a polygon of [longitude, latitude] points, drawn in the frame of the builds it belongs to ("scope", as for authored routes): within 180 degrees of the grid's centre, so in Europe, Asia and Africa (centred at 40 degrees east) Chukotka runs on past 180 degrees east. In a hard region there are no halts on long sections, no spurs out to hamlets, no stops at bare line ends, and a new line only gets a stop at a town or a city, not a village: the stops there are the stations actually mapped, the towns, and the ends of authored routes. Sparse stops are the point of a hard region, where the player has to stock up beforehand.

regions.note: Alaska (with its panhandle) and the Yukon, south to 60 degrees north east of the panhandle, from the continental rail network to the Bering Strait: Ashline's first really hard section (Likea, September 2026).

Yakutia east of the railway's end at Nizhny Bestyakh, Kolyma and Chukotka, to the Bering Strait tunnel and Wales: the Asian half of the hard section, from the first real railway to the strait (Likea, September 2026). North of 58 degrees, so the Baikal-Amur line, Sakhalin and the Amur-Yakutsk line up to Nizhny Bestyakh stay as they are.
